channel.title: Devin Desaulniers' Greater Vancouver Real Estate Blog
channel.description: Greater Vancouver and Tri-Cities, BC real estate news, explained in plain language by Devin Desaulniers, Real Estate Associate with Axford Real Estate.

item.title: Pet-friendly rentals in the Tri-Cities, BC: a newcomer's guide
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Looking for pet-friendly rentals in the Tri-Cities, BC? In BC a landlord can say no to pets, so the key is confirming the lease and any strata bylaws allow your pet before you sign. Here's what newcomers should know about pet deposits, strata limits and dog licences in Coquitlam, Port Moody and Port Coquitlam.

item.title: Burquitlam condo buyer guide: what should you know?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: A Burquitlam condo buyer should weigh Millennium Line access at Burquitlam Station, the City's transit-oriented redevelopment plan, and the strata file before removing subjects. Here is a plain-language guide for buyers and newcomers looking at Coquitlam's Burquitlam neighbourhood.

item.title: The Vancouver rent discount window is closing
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: After 34 months of year-over-year declines, Vancouver apartment and condo asking rents posted their first annual increase in October 2026 — a tiny +0.2% bump to $2,735. Urbanation says the window for cheaper rents is closing.

item.title: Relocating to Coquitlam, BC: first 30 days checklist
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Relocating to Coquitlam, BC? Use this first 30 days checklist for newcomers: set up BC Hydro, get a Compass Card for the Millennium Line, apply for MSP, register kids with SD43, and find Mundy Park and Como Lake.

item.title: Moving from Alberta to BC: a Tri-Cities, BC newcomer checklist
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Moving from Alberta to BC? Here's what changes when you land in the Tri-Cities, BC: your 90-day licence switch, the 30-day vehicle deadline, health coverage timing, BC's 7% PST, and rental rules that differ from Alberta's.

item.title: Metro Vancouver home sales fell 10% in October. What it means
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Greater Vancouver REALTORS® reports 2,024 Metro Vancouver home sales in October 2026, down 10.2% from a year ago, as a rate hike and a snap election kept buyers and sellers on the sidelines. My take for buyers, sellers and newcomers in the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Commuting from Port Moody to Vancouver: SkyTrain, WCE or car?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Commuting from Port Moody to Vancouver? Here's how the Millennium Line, the weekday West Coast Express and the drive along Barnet Highway or Lougheed Highway compare on time and fares, plus a checklist for newcomers choosing where to live in the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: What does a relocation agent in Port Moody do?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: A relocation agent in Port Moody helps newcomers find and secure a home before they arrive: searching, viewing homes for you, and reviewing the lease. Here's what the job covers in BC, what it doesn't, and how to check an agent's licence.

item.title: Most Metro Vancouver homes are selling below assessed value
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Zealty.ca data reported by the Vancouver Sun shows 18,168 of 24,426 homes sold in Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley this year closed below their 2026 BC Assessment value. My take for buyers and sellers in Greater Vancouver and the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Relocating to Port Moody, BC: a newcomer's guide
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Thinking about relocating to Port Moody, BC? Here's my newcomer's guide to getting around, the waterfront, and how to plan a rental search in the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Canada's snowiest cities. Vancouver? Just 38 cm a year
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: St. John's gets about 335 cm of snow in an average year. Vancouver gets just 38 cm, the lowest of 15 Canadian cities. Here's what that means if you're relocating, and why the hillsides are a different story.

item.title: New rental buildings are leasing up in Metro Vancouver. What renters gain
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Zonda Home data reported by the Vancouver Sun shows 59.5% of released purpose-built rental units in Metro Vancouver are leased, with about 900 units leasing a month and some buildings offering free rent. My take for renters and newcomers.

item.title: BC rental deposits and scams: what should newcomers know?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: In BC a landlord can ask for no more than half a month's rent as a security deposit, and must return it within 15 days of getting your forwarding address unless you agree otherwise or the RTB orders it. Here is how a newcomer can protect a deposit and spot a rental scam.

item.title: Doctors +43, politicians −48. Where would you rank REALTORS®?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Ipsos ranked 20 professions on trust for 2026. Doctors lead at +43 net trust and politicians trail at −48. REALTORS® aren't on the list at all, so I'm asking you where we'd land.

item.title: The Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.5%. What now?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: On October 28 the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by a quarter point to 2.5%, its first hike since July 2023. Here's what it means for buyers, sellers and renters in Greater Vancouver and the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: B.C. says \"not so fast\" to the viral $275 rent hike
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: A $275 rent hike went viral on X. In B.C., the 2026 cap for existing tenants is 2.3%, about $40 on $1,750 rent, once every 12 months with 3 full months' written notice on Form RTB-7.

item.title: 45% of Port Moody sales this year followed a failed listing
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: A Zealty analysis reported in local news found 45% of Port Moody homes sold in the first nine months of 2026 had a failed listing first, with 42% in Port Coquitlam and 38% in Coquitlam. Here's what that means for sellers and buyers in the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: B.C. has a new government. What it could mean for housing
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: The BC Conservatives under Lorne Doerkson are projected to win a majority. Politics aside, here's what they ran on for housing and what it could mean for buyers, sellers and renters in Greater Vancouver and the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Developers are sweetening new-home deals. Read the fine print.
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: The Globe and Mail reports B.C. developers are offering a $100,000 car or cash, $25,000 credits and mortgage subsidies to move unsold homes. My take for buyers in Greater Vancouver and the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: Can I rent in BC with no Canadian credit history?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Yes. In BC a landlord can screen you on ID, past-landlord references and proof of income, and the privacy commissioner says a credit check belongs near the end of the selection. Here is how a newcomer can build a strong rental application without Canadian credit.

item.title: Canada, a country of immigration: where we're born and where we go
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: About 8.8 million people living in Canada were born somewhere else, led by India, the Philippines and China. And of the 1.3 million Canadian-born people living abroad, 7 in 10 are in the U.S.

item.title: Traders put an 87% chance on a Bank of Canada hike
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: CBC News says overnight swap traders put an 87% chance on a quarter-point Bank of Canada hike on October 28, up from 70% earlier this week. The policy rate is still 2.25%.

item.title: The starter home isn't dead. It just moved into a condo.
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Everyone says the starter home is dead. My Greater Vancouver take: it isn't. In the Tri-Cities, BC, a first place is usually a condo or townhouse now, and the plan is still the same: get in, build equity, trade up later.

item.title: B.C. inflation held at 3.0% as Canada's rose to 3.1%
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Statistics Canada says Canada's CPI rose 3.1% in September 2026, while B.C. held at 3.0%. Shelter was up 1.8% and rent 2.8%. The Bank of Canada announces on October 28.

item.title: Where are B.C. jobs easiest to find right now?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: I mapped Statistics Canada's September 2026 three-month unemployment rates for every B.C. metro. Kamloops is 4.4%, Kelowna is 9.3%, and Metro Vancouver is 6.5%, in line with Canada.

item.title: Greater Vancouver home prices fell 4% in the third quarter
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Royal LePage says Greater Vancouver's aggregate home price was $1,148,100 in the third quarter of 2026, down 4.0% from a year earlier and 1.4% from the previous quarter.

item.title: Moving to Coquitlam from another province: what should I know about neighbourhoods, costs and the commute?
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Pick the Coquitlam neighbourhood that fits your commute, then budget the asking rent or the benchmark price for that kind of home. SkyTrain times, October 2025 rents and September 2026 sale prices.

item.title: Canada's Big Six posted $69.9B. Shop your mortgage.
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: Canada's Big Six posted $69.9 billion in reported net income for fiscal 2025, or C$69.861 billion combined. When a Greater Vancouver renewal or pre-approval comes up, shop it.

item.title: B.C.'s sales-to-active listings ratio was 12% in September
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: BCREA's September tables put B.C.'s sales-to-active listings ratio at 12%, with 43,940 homes listed, down 4.3% from a year ago. What that means in Greater Vancouver and the Tri-Cities, BC.

item.title: B.C. September home sales fell 8.9% from last year
item.dc:creator: Devin Desaulniers
item.description: The B.C. Real Estate Association says 5,254 homes sold in September 2026, down 8.9% from a year ago and 25.8% below the 10-year average for the month. The average price was $924,279.
